He attended four high schools in North Carolina, Maryland and Massachusetts before playing collegiately at [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]]. He was selected with the 22nd overall pick in the [[2005 NBA draft]] by the [[Denver Nuggets]], before playing with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], [[Indiana Pacers]], [[Toronto Raptors]], [[New Orleans Hornets]], [[Golden State Warriors]], [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[Brooklyn Nets]], [[New Orleans Pelicans]], and [[New York Knicks]]. ==High school career== Jack attended four high schools, including [[DeMatha Catholic High School]] and [[St. Vincent Pallotti High School]] in [[Maryland]], [[Mount Zion Christian Academy|Mount Zion Academy]] in [[North Carolina]], and [[Worcester Academy]] in [[Massachusetts]]. Considered a four-star recruit by [[Scout.com]], Jack was listed as the No. 9 point guard and the No. 40 player in the nation in 2002.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20150125073537/http://scouthoops.scout.com/player/11503n-jarrett-jack|title=Jarrett Jack Recruiting Profile}} ==College career== After high school, Jack played for [[Georgia Institute of Technology|Georgia Tech]] in [[Atlanta, Georgia|Atlanta]].{{Cite news |date=September 3, 2004 |title=All ACC Faces in the Crowd: Jarrett Jack |work=[[The Technique]] |url=http://nique.net/issues/2004-09-03/sports/6 |access-date=March 17, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929132254/http://nique.net/issues/2004-09-03/sports/6 |archive-date=September 29, 2007}} In his sophomore year (2003–04), he helped guide Georgia Tech to the NCAA Finals with 12.5 points and 5.1 assists a game. In his junior and final year at Georgia Tech he averaged 15.5 points, 4.8 rebounds and 4.5 assists. After forgoing his senior year of eligibility at Georgia Tech to enter the NBA draft, Jack graduated on December 13, 2014, receiving his degree in business management at commencement ceremonies in Atlanta.[http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/12/13/jarrett-jack-10-year-nba-veteran-graduates-from-georgia-tech/ Jarrett Jack, 10-year NBA veteran, graduates from Georgia Tech] ==Professional career== [[File:jarrett jack raptors v heat.jpg|thumb|left|Jack going for a layup in a game between the Toronto Raptors and the Miami Heat]] ===Portland Trail Blazers (2005–2008)=== After his junior year at Georgia Tech, he opted to enter the [[2005 NBA draft]] and was selected by the [[Denver Nuggets]] with the 22nd pick. On draft night, he was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for their 27th pick ([[Linas Kleiza]]) and 35th pick ([[Ricky Sánchez]]).{{Cite news |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=June 30, 2005 |title=2005 NBA Draft Grades |language=en |work=DraftExpress |url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/2005-NBA-Draft-Grades-1029/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180331225306/http://www.draftexpress.com/article/2005-NBA-Draft-Grades-1029/ |archive-date=March 31, 2018}}{{Cite news |last=Weitzman |first=Yaron |date=March 19, 2018 |title=Jarrett Jack's Wide Circle of Influence Extends to NBA Stars, Rappers and Beyond |language=en-US |work=[[Bleacher Report]] |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2762178-jarrett-jacks-wide-circle-of-influence-extends-to-nba-stars-rappers-and-beyond |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180331224631/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2762178-jarrett-jacks-wide-circle-of-influence-extends-to-nba-stars-rappers-and-beyond |archive-date=March 31, 2018}} As a rookie in 2005–06, Jack backed up [[Steve Blake]] and [[Sebastian Telfair]] as a point guard, getting limited minutes. Blake was traded to the Milwaukee Bucks and Telfair was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in a multi-player trade during the 2006 off-season. In their absence, Jack was named starting point guard by coach [[Nate McMillan]] for the 2006–07 season, dramatically increasing his minutes and stats. With Blake's return in 2007–08, however, Jack was once again relegated to [[sixth man]]. ===Indiana Pacers (2008–2009)=== On July 9, 2008, Jack was traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] along with [[Josh McRoberts]] and 2008 NBA draft pick [[Brandon Rush]] for [[Ike Diogu]] and [[Jerryd Bayless]].{{Cite web |date=July 9, 2009 |title=Pacers announce two trades; acquire seven players |url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers_trades_release_080709.html |access-date=July 13, 2009 |website=NBA.com}} ===Toronto Raptors (2009–2010)=== [[File:Jarrett-Jack-cropped.jpg|upright|thumb|Jack with the Toronto Raptors in 2010]] On July 13, 2009, Jack signed a 4-year, $20 million offer sheet with the Toronto Raptors.{{Cite web |date=July 13, 2009 |title=Raptors Sign Jack To Offer Sheet |url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/jack_offersheet_071309.html |access-date=July 14, 2009 |website=NBA.com}} The Pacers had seven days to match the offer, and they chose not to.{{Cite web |last=Wells |first=Mike |date=July 19, 2009 |title=Pacers won't match offer for Jarret Jack |url=http://www.indystar.com/article/20090719/SPORTS04/90719014/Pacers%2Bwon%2Bt%2Bmatch%2Boffer%2Bfor%2BJarret%2BJack |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140715040711/http://www.indystar.com/article/20090719/SPORTS04/90719014/Pacers%2Bwon%2Bt%2Bmatch%2Boffer%2Bfor%2BJarret%2BJack |archive-date=July 15, 2014 |access-date=July 19, 2009 |website=IndyStar.com}} ===New Orleans Hornets (2010–2012)=== On November 20, 2010, Jack was traded to the New Orleans Hornets, along with [[Marcus Banks]] and [[David Andersen]] for [[Peja Stojaković]] and [[Jerryd Bayless]].{{Cite web |date=November 20, 2010 |title=HORNETS ACQUIRE JACK, ANDERSON AND BANKS FROM RAPTORS |url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_acquire_jack_anderson_2010_11_20.html |access-date=November 21, 2010 |website=NBA.com}} ===Golden State Warriors (2012–2013)=== [[File:Jarrett Jack in March 2013.jpg|thumb|upright|Jack with the Golden State Warriors in 2013]] On July 11, 2012, Jack was traded to the Golden State Warriors in a three-team trade including the Philadelphia 76ers, who received Dorell Wright from Golden State. The Hornets received the right to [[Edin Bavčić]] in the deal.{{Cite web |date=July 11, 2012 |title=New Orleans Hornets Trade Jarrett Jack To Golden State Warriors |url=http://www.rantsports.com/courtcrusades/2012/07/11/new-orleans-hornets-trade-jarrett-jack-to-golden-state-warriors/ |access-date=July 11, 2012 |website=Rantsports.com |archive-date=May 31, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200531052643/http://www.rantsports.com/nba/2012/07/11/new-orleans-hornets-trade-jarrett-jack-to-golden-state-warriors/ |url-status=dead }} On February 22, 2013, Jack recorded a double-double with 30 points and 10 assists against the Spurs and became the first bench player to record such numbers since Magic Johnson in 1996.{{Cite web |date=February 22, 2013 |title=Jarrett Jack: NBS'a Best Sixth Man? |url=http://www.rantsports.com/nba/2013/02/23/golden-state-warrior-coach-pushing-jarrett-jack-for-nbas-best-sixth-man-award/ |access-date=February 22, 2013 |website=Rantsports.com |archive-date=September 24, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924085304/http://www.rantsports.com/nba/2013/02/23/golden-state-warrior-coach-pushing-jarrett-jack-for-nbas-best-sixth-man-award/ |url-status=dead }} At the end of season, Jack finished third in the Sixth Man of the Year voting.{{Cite web |date=April 22, 2013 |title=Knicks' J.R. Smith wins Kia Sixth Man Award |url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/04/22/smith-wins-sixth-man-award-release/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130426201858/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/04/22/smith-wins-sixth-man-award-release/index.html |archive-date=April 26, 2013 |access-date=April 22, 2013 |website=NBA.com}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2013–2014)=== On July 12, 2013, Jack signed a four-year, $25 million contract with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web | title=Cavaliers Sign Jack and Clark | website=NBA | date=2013-07-12 | url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/clark-jack-signing-130712 | access-date=2025-09-29}} On April 15, 2014, he was named the recipient of the ninth annual Austin Carr Good Guy Award. The award, named after Cavaliers legend [[Austin Carr]], is designed to recognize a Cavaliers player who is cooperative and understanding of the media.{{Cite web |date=April 15, 2014 |title=Jarrett Jack Wins Austin Carr Good Guy Award |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/good-guy-award-jack-140415 |access-date=January 2, 2016 |website=NBA.com}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2014–2016)=== On July 10, 2014, the Cleveland Cavaliers traded Jack to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in a three-team trade also involving the Boston Celtics, as they needed to clear cap space to re-sign [[LeBron James]]. This is the second trade involving Jack where the team trading him away received the rights to Edin Bavčić in return.[http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-acquire-jarrett-jack-and-sergey-karasev Brooklyn Nets Acquire Jarrett Jack and Sergey Karasev] Hours after graduating from Georgia Tech on December 13, 2014, Jack travelled to Charlotte to join his teammates for their game against the Hornets. In 20 minutes of action off the bench, he recorded 14 points, 5 assists, and 2 rebounds to help the Nets win 114–87.[http://www.nba.com/games/20141213/BKNCHA/gameinfo.html Johnson leads hot-shooting Nets over Hornets] On November 14, 2015, Jack scored a season-high 28 points in an overtime loss to the Golden State Warriors.{{Cite web |title=Curry leads Warriors past Nets 107–99 in overtime |website=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151114/BKNGSW/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151127112940/http://www.nba.com/games/20151114/BKNGSW/gameinfo.html |archive-date=November 27, 2015 |access-date=November 15, 2015}} On January 3, 2016, he was ruled out for the rest of the season with a torn anterior cruciate ligament and small medial meniscus tear in his right knee. He sustained the injury the previous night during the second half of the Nets' game at Boston.[http://www.nba.com/nets/news/jarrett-jack-medical-update Jarrett Jack Medical Update] On June 30, 2016, Jack was waived by the Nets.[http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2016/06/30/brooklyn-nets-waive-jarrett-jack Brooklyn Nets Waive Jarrett Jack] On July 15, 2016, Jack signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web |date=July 15, 2016 |title=Hawks Re-Sign Humphries, Add Jack And Delaney |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/features/hawks-re-sign-humphries-add-jack-delaney |access-date=July 15, 2016 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}} However, on October 20, 2016, he was waived by the Hawks due to injury. He had been unable to practice during training camp due to torn right knee ligaments he suffered in 2015–16, and subsequently sat out all seven of the Hawks' exhibition games during the preseason.{{Cite web |date=October 20, 2016 |title=Hawks Request Waivers On Jarrett Jack |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-request-waivers-jarrett-jack |access-date=October 20, 2016 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}{{Cite web |last=Vivlamore |first=Chris |date=October 20, 2016 |title=Hawks waive veteran Jack, roster at 17 |url=http://www.ajc.com/sports/basketball/hawks-waive-veteran-jack-roster/rN2j0EB24I04B3wvqRh2wI/ |access-date=October 20, 2016 |website=AJC.com}} ===Return to New Orleans (2017)=== On February 24, 2017, Jack signed a 10-day contract with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], returning to the franchise for a second stint.{{Cite web |date=February 24, 2017 |title=Pelicans Sign Jarrett Jack |url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-sign-jarrett-jack |access-date=February 24, 2017 |website=NBA.com}} However, on March 3, 2017, he was ruled out for four to six weeks after suffering a right lateral meniscus tear.{{Cite web |date=March 3, 2017 |title=Jarrett Jack Injury Update |url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/jarrett-jack-injury-update-3-3-17 |access-date=March 3, 2017 |website=NBA.com}} ===New York Knicks (2017–2018)=== On September 15, 2017, Jack signed with the [[New York Knicks]].{{Cite web |date=September 15, 2017 |title=Knicks Sign Jarrett Jack |url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/features/knicks-sign-jarrett-jack |access-date=September 15, 2017 |website=NBA.com}} On November 24, 2017, he had 10 points and a season-high 14 assists against the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. On December 10, 2017, also against the Hawks, Jack scored a season-high 19 points.{{Cite web |title=Jarrett Jack 2017–18 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/jackja01/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=January 7, 2018 |website=Basketball-Reference.com}} On January 10, 2018, he recorded his first triple-double in six years with 16 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 122–119 double overtime loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite web |date=January 10, 2018 |title=Markkanen, Dunn help Bulls outlast Knicks 122–119 in Double Overtime |url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975353 |access-date=January 10, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}} Four days later, he set a new season high with 22 points in a 123–118 overtime loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{Cite web |date=January 14, 2018 |title=Davis (48 points, 17 rebounds), Pelicans beat Knicks in OT |url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975381 |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}} Jack signed with the Pelicans on September 19, 2018,{{Cite web |date=September 19, 2018 |title=Pelicans sign Jarrett Jack |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-sign-jarrett-jack-091918 |access-date=September 19, 2018 |website=NBA.com}} before being waived on October 13.{{Cite web |date=October 13, 2018 |title=Pelicans waive Green and Jack |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-green-and-jack |access-date=October 13, 2018 |website=NBA.com}} ===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2019–2020)=== On March 5, 2019, Jack was acquired by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{Cite web |date=March 5, 2019 |title=Sioux Falls Skyforce Acquire NBA Veteran Jarrett Jack |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/sioux-falls-skyforce-acquire-nba-veteran-jarrett-jack/ |access-date=March 10, 2019 |website=NBA.com}} In his lone appearance for the Skyforce, Jack tore the ACL and lateral meniscus as well as spraining the MCL in his left knee, which ruled him out for the rest of the season.{{Cite web |last=Ira Winderman |date=March 14, 2019 |title=Jarrett Jack, who signed Skyforce]].{{Cite web |date=November 26, 2019 |title=SKYFORCE ACQUIRES JARRETT JACK |url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-acquires-jarrett-jack-2/ |access-date=November 26, 2019
